reason: The terminal client treated a supervisor Core's 202 saved-request receipt as the final answer: a first message on a cold project worker was reported as 'Connection lost. Nothing was resent' and restored to the draft while Core ran it, and mutations returned the receipt as the resource (a rename reported the old title as saved). AsyncApi now follows runtime/requests/{id}/response like the GUI, never resending; streamed submissions report the saved state, attach to the saved turn, block a duplicate new-conversation send, and /follow or /status resolve the receipt. Selected: the transport and shell unit contracts (including new receipt cases), the TUI presentation suite for the submission label, and real paired TLS LAN Core cases that send, stream, mutate with idempotency keys and recover remembered chats.
exclusions: No full suites. No frontend, native or Playwright changes; only the separate Python terminal client changed, so browser viewport projects do not exercise it. Other tests/v3/test_terminal_core.py cases and tests/test_terminal_pty.py are not selected: 6 of them fail identically on pristine origin/main locally (scroll [52-18], wide layout, direct chats/reconnect, loading while opening, polling, queue/detach/approval), so they cannot prove this change; the selected four pass on main and on this branch. Supervisor 202 receipts cannot occur on the create_app fixture Core; that path is covered by MockTransport unit cases plus real supervisor scratch-Core evidence in the PR body, not executed by CI. No live provider calls or Core deployment.
